It seems to me an update coordinator designed to limit how far we see into the future is not a great match for a calendar entity where upcoming events may be arbitrary far into the future.

To my understanding, the design used in the `caldav` integration is very similar to the design used in other integrations, so I suspect the same problem exists in other integrations too.

I agree with @allenporter a new config entry option is not a great way to fix the issue.

~~Instead of adding a config entry option to `caldav`, should we make the time range used to set the `event` property configurable via an entity option?~~
Edit: I don't think this was a good idea

Or, perhaps better, should we make the calendar coordinators smarter, so they query the API again with date further in the future if the list of events come back empty?

Edit: Radarr calendar has such a loop: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/e2dd88be6ef0792b764b0bb39374ffe0b0d511eb/homeassistant/components/radarr/coordinator.py#L153-L162

The timestamp of the next known events could be remembered by the coordinator in-between updates so the repeated querying does not happen on every update.

> Or, perhaps better, should we make the calendar coordinators smarter, so they query the API again with date further in the future if the list of events come back empty?
> 
> Edit: Radarr calendar has such a loop:
> 
> https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/e2dd88be6ef0792b764b0bb39374ffe0b0d511eb/homeassistant/components/radarr/coordinator.py#L153-L162
> 
> The timestamp of the next known events could be remembered by the coordinator in-between updates so the repeated querying does not happen on every update.

I do think some kind of adaptive querying and memory is the right balance. (it may need to still query a large time range since new events can be added within that range, but the larger point is to remember a time duration hint and not need to issue so many queries every time, agreed)

Why make things so overcomplicated trying to create automations that are prone to fail anyway instead of simply letting the user decide how many days in the future should be considered?
After all, this is already implemented in YAML. Just add that option to the UI. Simple as that.

@thatso the calendar's event property represents the next upcoming event. There's absolutely no reason why the user should have to configure the period in which an integration searches for the next event.

@emontnemery ... unless that period is unexpectedly limited to the next day only (or 7 days). After all, that's why I opened the corresponding bug #108003 in the first place.
I am simply suggesting the most logical and easiest to implement solution. Maybe check the initial discussion.
Again: why not let the user decide?
How could you possibly determine a sane automated search limit? Maybe I have a maintenance reminder that repeats once every five years? What if a next event does not exist yet? Will you search in an infinite future range?

@thatso it's not about letting the user decide. It's about it being unnecessarily complicated to require the user to hunt in the config entry options for a setting which makes the calendar entity's state reflect the next event.

I'm trying to follow this conversation, and it looks like there is a suggestion to not allow setting max days, but instead have the integration search into the future to find the next day, no matter how far in the future it is.

Doesn't that still pose a max days problem, since future days are (theoretically) infinite? Radarr breaks at 45 days. But there may be users who want that to be 90 days, or 365 days.

It may be worth having a much larger range than the current default and implementing an iterable search like Radarr has, but it still seems that the day value would benefit from being a config option.

Maybe, default to 45 (like Radarr) and then allow users to set that further to the future, if they so desired.

@ViViDboarder of course this poses the risk of an infinite loop as I've stated earlier like a fresh entry that simply does not have any occurrence at all.
I know I sound like a broken record but for some reason beyond any logic the simple and obvious solution to let the user decide the time range gets constantly denied and even downvoted.
Anyway: it has been seven months and this stupid issue is going nowhere near any finish because seemingly some _1337 coderz_ in their high tower want to know better than the user, so I'm officially out by now.
Did I mention I'm sick and tired of this attitude? It is said open source thrives on participation. If so, this is a fine example how things should not work out.
BTW: surely the same people will explain now in great length why I'm wrong. Go ahead: knock yourself out. As said: I no longer care.

issue_context.title: obvious solution denied: CalDAV entities setup in UI ignore events more than 6 days in the future
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I have a Nextcloud calendar with single monthly events for garbage collection. These events show up in the calendar view but only trigger the corresponding entity when they are no more than 6 days in the future. It does not matter if they are all day events or have start and stop times.
Today is January, 14th. A test entry for the 20th shows up in the calendar and triggers the entity:

![1](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/40745263/770c47bb-856b-4fce-9dda-0cf4cba7fd95)

![2](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/40745263/eed83527-f092-4d69-bb3c-9e5d80f70860)

If I change this event's date to one day later or any other date more than 6 days in the future, it still shows in the calendar but the entity stays empty:

![3](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/40745263/cab765f6-c61f-45ec-a785-49726acdf63c)

![4](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/40745263/4994d24e-9b07-407e-be11-527aff126bf5)

Notice that besides the test entries there is a regular entry for February, 3rd, which also does not show in the entity.

![5](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/40745263/7f1cc9db-d067-4ca1-a60d-a0c3a1fee1c3)



### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2024.1.3

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

CalDAV

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/caldav

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

I've reloaded the CalDAV integration and also rebooted HA between the test entries.
The described error happens only when adding the CalDAV integration via UI.
If I add it manually via YAML and specifically state `days: 60` the entity attributes contain the event scheduled for the next month as expected.
I suspect the reason lies in line 45 of `core/homeassistant/components/caldav/calendar.py`:
`CONFIG_ENTRY_DEFAULT_DAYS = 7`

review_comments:
I think its reasonable to change the default in the future when not set, so perhaps not set this?

As an alternative: I am curious what you were planning to set the # of days? I was curious if we should just increase the default.  I saw this before at 7 and thought that it was pretty low. Not sure if it would solve your problem to increase the default and not offer this as an option.

> I think its reasonable to change the default in the future when not set, so perhaps not set this?

this is just to add a value to the config entry options if there is no one, yet.

> As an alternative: I am curious what you were planning to set the # of days? I was curious if we should just increase the default. I saw this before at 7 and thought that it was pretty low. Not sure if it would solve your problem to increase the default and not offer this as an option.

The default for YAML config is [1 day](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/4d75940cd21d183414c290c6c778bb75936a0763/homeassistant/components/caldav/calendar.py#L70) and changeable by the user on demand.
When configuring via UI, than we actually set 7 days which might be enough for many (_most_) of the users, but sometimes it is to less (_see #108003_).
So i thought to make it configurable again, would offer the most flexibility to the users.
My own use case is my birthdays calendar - i don't have much friends, therefor not much entries in there 🙈😁 so it happens that next date will be a few more days/weeks far
Would there be a down side if we just set the default to 30 days? or 60 days?

yeah, i think it might still not be enough for some users. tbh the link issue is the only one i know complaining about it, so i think the 7 days is already ok for most users. Maybe we should just mention the 7 days and the possibility to change it in the docs?
one downside of statically increasing to 60 or 90 days, it might result in higher load on CalDAV servers, especial on well filled calendars 🤔
If we can find a default that works for most folks (e.g. 14 days, 30 days) that seems like it be ideal to not need extra configuration options.

please don't get me wrong, but why not give the user the possibility to change this on it's own preferences or needs?
Sure, we can also increase the default to 30 which might be also good for most users, but also might increase the load on their caldav servers (_since more events might be returned_) and and their HA instances (_since more events needs to be checked which is the very next one_).
Further i think most users are already satisfied with the 7 days, since we we got only the one issue till now.

My general impression is we want to not offer additional configuration options unless needed, and not necessarily support use cases that are far outside the norm. If we can find a balance of end user simplicity and performance then that would be ideal. If its not possible to find that middle ground because its too expensive, then its not possible i guess.

(Perhaps bad idea: could also be adaptive (first try 7 days, then 14, then max 32 if no events are found).)

@allenporter: I am the one who opened #108003 and I certainly would not call said garbage reminder once a month "far outside the norm". In fact, I initially was happy with the HA update that made the CalDAV integration available via GUI only to spend days wondering why my calendar did not work until I found out about this limitation of days which was nowhere documented.
Besides: just because I'm the only one who opened a bug report does not mean numerous others also fell for this limitation and silently just gave up and reverted to the manual YAML way.

If you read my above responses I'm not against solving this use case.  I just don't want to add more configuration options. Instead you'd be surprised it didn't work and have to hunt down a config option you didn't know existed. We should just make it work for you out or the box with no additional action on your part.

I'm in favor of solving this in a few ways proposed above... either increasing the limit (is this really an efficiency problem? I'm skeptical) or doing something adaptive and more efficient. 

Happy to be overruled here by other code approvers, that's just my 2 cents.

The logical solution would be the one initially supposed by @mib1185: an options dialogue letting the user decide how many days to check, maybe with a note that too many days might increase the server load (which of course depends on the infrastructure, overall number of calendars and individual entries to check and such). To top it: a separate days chooser for each calendar, maybe as simple as entities after the initial setup.
Anyway, it should be emphasized in the docs that only one single day is taken into account. Currently, it is only mentioned in the [manual configuration steps](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/caldav/) and very easily overlooked, especially if someone uses the GUI integration and thus will most likely never get the idea to check these manual steps. At least that is what I did or better did not before I opened what I believed to be a bug report.
I will happily update the current docs accordingly, but it seems more efficient to wait for the outcome of this proposed change to avoid the need to update the docs again shortly afterwards. :wink:

I'm still on the point, that having this option does not overwhelm our users, because it is not part of the integration setup phase (_config flow_), but can later be changed by the user if needed (_options flow_).
Also, as mentioned before, I think the default setting of 7 days is suitable for most of our users, so only a few users will need this option and then have it. Last but not least we could describe the options in the docs (_eq. we do in [AVM Fritz!Tools](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/fritz#integration-options)_) - i'm happy to update the docs accordingly 🙂
